You are reviewing the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim (branch llamacpp) for STRUCTURAL refactor candidates.
First read /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md to understand the architecture.

HARD RULES:
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, build, or run anything (no make, no scripts, no ./andesim). Baseline test runs are using the build tree right now. Use Read/Grep/Glob and read-only git commands only.
- Structural = behavior-preserving: dead code, duplication, needless complexity, stale comments/docs that contradict the code, naming that hides intent, repo hygiene. NOT rewrites for taste. The repo just went through a history cleanup, so it is fairly clean; report only what you can defend with evidence. An empty findings list is a valid answer.
- If you find what looks like a real BUG (behavior wrong), report it with category "bug-report" - it will be handled separately, not as a refactor.
- For every finding give: file (repo-relative), line, category, title, one-paragraph detail with EVIDENCE (what you read/grepped), safety (why removing/changing it cannot change behavior), verify_with (which existing test or check proves it after the change).
- Cite real file paths and line numbers you actually read. No speculation.

Your assigned scope (do not wander into other subsystems except to grep for references):
qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c (764 lines) + qemu_plugin/Makefile. Do NOT review the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h. Look for dead drain paths, duplicated CSR-list iteration that should use the X-macro, stale comments about removed QEMU2 leg.

Return your findings as the structured output.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. - iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,

Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. 1	# Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
2	# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
3	# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
4	#
5	# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
6	# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
7	# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
8	# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   make            # build both
12	#   make clean
13	#
14	# Output (in this directory):
15	#   libhybrid_handoff.so    -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
16	#   libhotIterationLoop.so  -- hot inner-loop detector (`andesim profile`)
17	
18	CC ?= gcc
19	
20	GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
21	GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)
22	
23	CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
24	HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
25	# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
26	QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
27	INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
28	LDFLAGS := -shared
29	LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)
30	
31	.PHONY: all clean
32	
33	all: libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so
34	
35	libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
36	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
37	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
38	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h \
39	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/write_mask.h
40		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)
41	
42	# hotIterationLoop is standalone: it needs only qemu-plugin.h + glib, not
43	# HYBRID_INCLUDE.
44	libhotIterationLoop.so: hotIterationLoop.c
45		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotIterationLoop.c $(LIBS)
46	
47	clean:
48		rm -f libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so
49
